name: network
label: Network
description: A living view of the UniFi network: WAN state, speed and latency, every device with its uplink, every client with its band, signal and current traffic, new devices first seen recently, and the issues worth fixing - plus a 3D map you can turn, with traffic flowing along the links. The data comes from the UniFi connector (Settings > Integrations) and is sampled every 30 seconds in the background.

steps: Everything here comes from the UniFi connector: console URL and an API key in Settings > Integrations (the same fields on the Integrations page). The Network page never asks for credentials of its own.

The header is the WAN: up, IP, current throughput and latency, plus the last speedtest. The cards count clients and devices, list the issues (offline APs, weak signals, unhappy clients, WAN problems) and show devices first seen in the last day. The tables are the detail; the 3D map is the same data as a picture - drag to turn it, wheel to zoom, hover for a name, click for the numbers.

Each client is a dot around the AP or switch it is using; the number and speed of the particles on its link scale with its current throughput, so a busy client is visibly busy. Wired, 5 GHz and 2.4 GHz are different colours.

The first time a MAC is seen it is recorded in jobs\network-known.json and a notice is raised (the same toast as notify). The New devices card lists anything first seen in the last 24 hours, so a strange device is visible without hunting.
fixes: The UniFi connector is not configured or not answering: check the Integrations page first (console URL, API key, site default). The page shows the connector's error instead of an empty map.
The snapshot is stale or the poller has not run yet: press refresh (it checks on demand when the state is over 90 seconds old). If UniFi answers but clients are zero, they really are zero.
Rates are the controller's own bytes-per-second for the moment of the sample, not a speedtest. Use the WAN card's speedtest numbers for line capacity.
